newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance credit facility extended.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance credit facility extended.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Wednesday that Bank of America agreed to extend its $50 million credit facility through January 6, 1998.

The facility is subject to the same terms and conditions as the existing agreement, including the extension of creditor waivers. The waivers, which expired June 10, enable the company to pledge assets to collateralize the BankAmerica Corp unit's loan.
The company said it continues negotiations to obtain the extension of creditor waivers.
No funds are currently outstanding to Bank of America under the credit facility, and none have been outstanding since the line was repaid in May, Mercury said.
Mercury said cash flow position is positive, and the company does not anticipate the need to borrow any funds at the current time or in the near future.

"In fact, we never utilized more than $10 million of the line for operational purposes," William Brandt Jr, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement. "Indeed, we have been able to pay expenses from cash flow, including interest on all of our indebtedness."
Mercury said it remains committed to a timely completion of the 1996 audit of financial statements as early as possible, and in line with estimates released in April.
First quarter results should be released soon thereafter.
